title: Test: every transferred cell-voltage value is integrity-checked before any decision consumes it, and every published value carries a usable age

standards_mappings.reference: SYS.4 (system integration testing) and SYS.5 (system verification)
standards_mappings.rationale: This measure is the verification the system requirement states as needed. Its oracle is declared and distinguishable and its execution status is declared; neither constitutes evidence that the requirement is met.

Verification of the system requirement as written, against its own acceptance criteria. The requirement carries a reconstructed ASIL allocation in the reference project; this measure verifies the requirement's behaviour and asserts nothing about whether that allocation is correct.

lifecycle_status_note: Set to the value above because no human has reviewed or approved this record. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation (schema, link, provenance and consistency checks run by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py) and is not a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: Authored because FB2-SYS-SYR-000001 had no verifies link in either direction, so the corpus's own audit reported it as an unverified system requirement. The measure separates the two of the requirement's four criteria that the pinned source can be falsified against from the acquisition-rate criterion, which cannot, and declares the oracle kind of each.

objective: Confirm two of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001's four acceptance criteria against the pinned source's own mechanism: that the integrity of every transferred value is decided before any decision uses it, and that each published value carries an age that can be read. The integrity criterion is judged against LTC_CheckPec's per-LTC comparison and the fact that a PEC mismatch marks the cell-voltage entry invalid before the parsed values reach the database; the age criterion is judged against the database header timestamp that every write path stamps. The acquisition-rate criterion is deliberately NOT verified here: its figure is a modelled parameter and is covered by a separate measure with a different oracle.
preconditions: The reference project's AFE driver is initialised and a measurement cycle has completed at least once.
The database is initialised so that a write stamps the block header.
The AFE plausibility entry is available for the range check.

environment.hardware: POSIX host (Linux) running the unit-test build, with the AFE driver and the database linked and the SPI interface stubbed
environment.software: foxBMS 2 application firmware built with the unit-test configuration
environment.configuration: conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml with FOXBMS_AFE_DRIVER_LTC=1u, which is the configuration the repository's own unit-test build selects

stimuli.signal: AFE SPI response frame with a deliberately corrupted PEC byte
stimuli.value: one frame per corrupted cell group, PEC recomputed so that exactly one LTC in the frame mismatches
stimuli.timing: one injection per measurement cycle, for 100 consecutive cycles

stimuli.value: read of the cell-voltage block header after every write
the value a supervisory decision reads for the affected cell

steps.action: Run 100 measurement cycles with uncorrupted frames and record the PEC validity flag and the header timestamp for each published block.
steps.expected: Every cycle reports PEC valid and every published block carries a non-zero header timestamp.

steps.action: Run 100 measurement cycles in which exactly one LTC's PEC is corrupted, and record the PEC validity flag, the per-cell invalid flag and the value a supervisory decision reads.
steps.expected: The corrupted LTC's PEC validity flag is false, its per-cell invalid flag is true, and no decision reads a value for that cell that is not marked invalid.

steps.action: Suppress the database write for one cycle and read the header timestamp again.
steps.expected: The header timestamp does not advance for the suppressed cycle, so the age of the last published value is observable rather than inferred.

steps.action: Compare the age implied by the header timestamp against the number of measurement cycles elapsed.
steps.expected: The age increases monotonically and by one acquisition period per elapsed cycle.

oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is the mechanism the pinned source itself defines, read from the code rather than from the item's output. 'A transferred value whose recomputed packet error code differs from the received one is marked invalid, and an invalid value is not consumed by a decision' is what LTC_CheckPec (ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878) and the invalidCellVoltage flag it sets at line 641 do. 'A published block carries an age' is what DATA_CopyData (database.c:164-196) does when it copies previousTimestamp and sets timestamp from OS_GetTickCount on every write. Both properties are therefore falsifiable against the source without running the item, which is what makes them usable as oracles at all.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: no block header was read from a running system in this authoring pass, so the property is asserted from the code and not yet observed. It is not an analytical model: no arithmetic model of the integrity path was computed. It is not a synthetic assumption: the property asserted is a property of the code that exists, not an assumption about this programme.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: It does not prove the corrupted frame is rejected at the AFE rather than merely marked, and it does not prove any downstream decision in the reference project actually consults the invalid flag rather than the raw value. It says nothing about the acquisition rate, which is the fourth acceptance criterion and is covered elsewhere.
oracle_detail.residual_risk: A source-grounded oracle rests on the code doing what this pass read it to do. If the invalid flag were cleared downstream before a decision reads the block, this oracle would still pass.

cleanup: Restore the stubbed SPI interface, re-run one uncorrupted cycle to confirm the driver is back in its nominal state, and drop the injected frames.
regression_selection: Re-run on every change to LTC_CheckPec, to the invalidCellVoltage handling, to the database write path or to the header timestamp update. Also re-run whenever a new decision path is added that reads the cell-voltage block, because this oracle says nothing about how that path uses the invalid flag.
limitations: The integrity and age criteria are verified structurally against the source; the acquisition-rate criterion of the same requirement is not verified by this measure and is not silently counted as verified.
Nothing has been executed. The paired execution record carries execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked'.

The corrupted-frame injection requires a controllable SPI stub, which the unit-test build provides for the driver but which this corpus has not run; the measure states the capability it depends on rather than assuming it.
This is a synthetic measure. It establishes nothing about the real foxBMS product and no ASIL is claimed for it.
